title: cicd.yaml
description: Developer-facing pipeline configuration. This is the only file app teams edit to control their CI/CD pipelines - it never contains Tekton, YAML pipeline steps, or infrastructure details. Validated fail-fast by the validate-cicd-config Task before any other pipeline step runs.

agent.description: Named build agent image from the platform catalog. Not a raw image reference - keeps step code portable and centrally patchable. Still required even when `script` is omitted, since unit tests always run inside this image regardless of build strategy.

script.description: Build script the platform runs inside the agent image before packaging. Must be bash. Omit entirely for teams doing the whole build inside a multi-stage Dockerfile - the separate build-source stage is skipped and kaniko builds `dockerfile` directly. No default: presence/absence is the switch, so it can't silently mean 'skip' via an unrelated typo.

enabled.description: Persistent dependency-download cache for build-source (npm's package cache / Maven's local repository, not node_modules/target itself - see docs/cicd-yaml-reference.md). No `type` field: derived from `agent`'s prefix (nodejs-* -> npm, openjdk-* -> maven), not a second, redundantly-declarable field. Keyed by a hash of the relevant lockfile (package-lock.json/pom.xml) so a dependency change invalidates the cache automatically. A no-op (logged, not an error) for agents without cache support yet (python-*/go-1.22). Teams with no build.script (whole build inside a multi-stage Dockerfile) get layer caching for free from kaniko instead.

size.description: T-shirt size for this app's own cache PVC (small=1Gi, medium=2.5Gi, large=5Gi, xlarge=8Gi - same dictionary as the old cd-pipelines-user Helm chart's buildSpec.cacheSize). One PVC per app, not shared across a tenant's apps, specifically so this can vary per app. Chosen at onboarding time, not resizable live afterward - kind-observe's default storage class has allowVolumeExpansion: false, so changing this later means recreating the PVC (and losing its cached content), not a live resize.

suite.description: Name of the Testkube/test suite to run against the dev deployment.

strategy.description: deployment = native k8s Deployment rollout; rollout = Argo Rollouts (canary/blue-green).

ttl.description: How long an ephemeral environment lives after its last successful deploy before automatic teardown.

governance.description: Quality/security gates. In this phase of the platform these are STUBS - they always report a stub result and are rendered as such in Grafana. Toggling them on prepares your pipeline shape for when real implementations land; it does not enable real enforcement yet.

scanResults.description: Shift-left notifications from sast-scan/image-scan the moment each real scan produces a result, separate from the general build/test/deploy/release pass-fail notification above (which stays on whenever slack.enabled is true). Only takes effect when slack.enabled is also true. Defaults on (matching the pipeline's own default real-scan behavior), but a tenant that finds these too frequent/verbose can turn just this off without losing the general per-stage notifications.

pipeline.description: Stage graph. Each entry names a stage from the fixed platform stage set and what it runs after. This does not define arbitrary DAGs - it toggles/orders a known, finite set of stages (build, test, deploy, release).

after.description: Name of the stage (optionally suffixed :env, e.g. deploy:staging) this stage runs after. Omit for the first stage.

env.description: Required for deploy/release stages: which environment from deploy.lowerEnvironments/upperEnvironments this instance targets.

approvalRequired.description: Only meaningful on release stages targeting an upper environment.
